items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: I asked him about Begg Speederbeck. I said, are you familiar with him?

ctx.x: Yeah, he liked them. And the funny thing about that, see, I had, I'd been pretty much out of Bud Rack time and enough. To about 1925, I'd bought a few records now and then, most with piano records. But in 1925, I started going to night school, and I was working daytime, and I didn't have time for anything else. So I dropped out of my life entirely, almost, to music. I didn't play much. My nephew came low, he was playing, and I wouldn't pay much attention. So, I started to tell something I'm going to forget. What…

I asked him about Begg Speederbeck. I said, are you familiar with him? He said, yes. I said, have you heard him play? He said, yes, I heard him play. I said, well, was he good? He said, yes, he was good. He wasn't as good as they say he was. That's about his course. He said, no, I've never heard him play. He said, yes, he was good. He said, he wasn't as good as they say.

I was close at the time. I was 38 and was here. I was 20 years old. I was asking him about Frank Teschmaker and all these people. They were all right, but he said, these boys like Jimmy Noon and Umar Simeon. It was so much better. There was no comparison. It's true, of course.
